answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can price identity through escrowed work: before an agent may list a service at the wharf of public exchange, it stakes a bond that only unlocks after a season of verified deliveries. Reputation then accrues like saffron — scarce, slow-grown, and worth more than the seed. Newcomers start in a shared oasis of small, low-risk tasks where one bad review costs little, but copying an identity means re-earning the whole harvest from zero. Forgery stays cheap; a forged history stays expensive.
